closest_prior_work.difference: Studies deterministic operator and functional minimization, not stochastic mini-batch training. Does not report held-out accuracy or a fixed update-count budget, and its test problems are not comparable to this logistic-regression setup.

closest_prior_work.title: An Improved Analysis of Stochastic Gradient Descent with Momentum
closest_prior_work.overlap: Analyzes SGD with momentum (m_k = β m_{k-1} + (1−β) g_k, x_{k+1} = x_k − α m_k) on smooth objectives, with phased parameter schedules (LIT-0002 lines 24, 28).
closest_prior_work.difference: Theory-first convergence bounds under smoothness assumptions, with numerical experiments only in support. Makes no claim about accuracy at a fixed update count on a classification task. Verification is unverified because arXiv and Semantic Scholar returned HTTP 429, so identity was not confirmed by lookup.

closest_prior_work.title: Communication-Efficient Stochastic Gradient Descent Ascent with Momentum Algorithms
closest_prior_work.overlap: Both use a momentum-based stochastic gradient method (LIT-0003 line 35).
closest_prior_work.difference: Distributed stochastic minimax optimization with compressed communication and convergence-rate analysis for nonconvex-strongly-concave objectives. Not a single-machine SGD-versus-heavy-ball accuracy comparison.

review_payload.delta_sentence: At an equal one-epoch update budget (38 updates, same data, microbatch and reference learning rate), heavy-ball SGD yields higher held-out accuracy on the 400-sample explore set, a fixed-budget accuracy endpoint that the cited papers do not report.

document.title: critical_review CAND-0001
document.summary: claude_code anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5: proceed

named_risks: Learning-rate confound: the momentum run may use a different or tuned learning rate than the frozen reference (lr 0.005), so any accuracy gain may reflect step size rather than momentum. The pre-registered learning-rate design required by docs/project/min-setup.v1.md was not visible in the cited files.
Statistical power: 1 pp equals about 4 of 400 explore examples, with only 3 paired seeds (42-44) and 38 updates per seed. A result above or below the 1.0 pp threshold could be noise.

Unfrozen framework: docs/project/min-setup.v1.md states the runner, artifact fields, counts, pairing and decision rules are still pending root-task verification, so results could be produced before the comparison is fixed.
Confirmation independence: success requires confirmation on c1 (seeds 1042-1044), and c2 for changed candidates. Reusing explore data for selection would invalidate the claim.

Unverifiable implementation: code/configs/reference.json and code/toytrain/methods.py could not be read from this review context, so the reference settings, momentum coefficient and update rule are unchecked.

Literature support is partial: LIT-0002 (Liu, Gao, Yin 2020) is unverified because arXiv and Semantic Scholar returned HTTP 429, and its note says momentum gives no universal empirical advantage at a fixed learning rate. LIT-0003 concerns distributed minimax and does not test this setting.
Scope: protocol eval_type is synthetic_proxy, so any positive result applies only to this synthetic logistic-regression task and cannot be generalized.
review_payload.cheapest_discriminating_experiment: Before any candidate run, freeze a small pre-registered learning-rate set for both reference SGD and heavy-ball momentum, then run seeds 42-44 on code/data/explore.jsonl through the existing runner. Confirm the reference config and momentum update match the min-setup and standard heavy-ball form, and check whether the paired accuracy difference exceeds 1.0 pp at matched learning rates and stays positive across the set. If the gain vanishes at matched learning rates, the candidate is a step-size effect rather than a momentum effect.
missing_evidence: code/configs/reference.json contents (learning rate, batch, accum, update count) to confirm they match docs/project/min-setup.v1.md
code/toytrain/methods.py implementation of the momentum update and its coefficient, to confirm it is standard heavy-ball
The pre-registered momentum learning-rate design referenced by min-setup.v1.md, showing it was fixed before any run
Root-task verification and freeze of the runner (code/toytrain/run.py), artifact manifest fields, counts, and paired statistics
Verified metadata for LIT-0002 (arXiv 2007.07989), which is currently unverified
Explore, confirmation (c1, c2) and train split SHA256 identities from code/data/splits.json, to confirm independence and the declared train_split_id train@417cb63ca377
Any prior run or sanity-baseline evidence showing the paired-difference variance across seeds at 38 updates

document.title: novelty_precheck CAND-0002
document.summary: claude_code anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5: PROCEED_WITH_CAUTION

closest_prior_work.title: Why Warmup the Learning Rate? Underlying Mechanisms and Improvements
closest_prior_work.overlap: Studies linear LR warmup for SGD and reports that its main benefit is letting training tolerate a larger target learning rate, a stability-type effect. Warmup benefit is shown to depend on initialization and parameterization, and extra warmup time gives marginal gains (PDF p.2).
closest_prior_work.difference: Targets deep networks (FCN, ResNet, Transformer) on CIFAR, TinyImageNet and WikiText, not a synthetic one-epoch task. Does not evaluate a first-10% linear ramp with one-epoch accuracy under a paired-seed protocol. LIT-0005 states it does not claim the 10% schedule or a one-epoch accuracy gain.

review_payload.delta_sentence: Unlike Kalra & Barkeshli (arXiv:2406.09405), which studies warmup mechanisms for deep networks, this candidate tests whether a linear warmup over the first 10% of updates raises paired-seed accuracy for SGD on a fixed synthetic one-epoch logistic-regression task (protocol and metric in docs/project/protocol.v1.json and metric-spec.v1.json); the claim must be restated as an accuracy effect, since accuracy is the only metric and cannot show 'stabilize'.

document.title: critical_review CAND-0002
document.summary: claude_code anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5: proceed

named_risks: Claim says warmup makes training 'steadier' but the only metric is accuracy (metric-spec.v1.json); stability cannot be tested with the declared metric
Warmup target learning rate and post-warmup schedule are not specified; without them the candidate is not operationally defined
10% of 38 steps is about 3.8 steps; rounding rule is unspecified
Warmup can change effective step size relative to the frozen reference SGD, confounding the comparison with learning-rate and update-count differences that goal.v1.md excludes
LIT-0005 concerns deep networks and explicitly does not establish a fixed 10% warmup for single synthetic tasks; it cannot support the candidate
With min_pairs 3 and a 1 pp practical threshold on 400 eval examples, paired-seed noise may exceed the effect size
Brief's ../code/ path does not resolve; methods.py and the reference config could not be inspected
review_payload.cheapest_discriminating_experiment: Restate the claim as an accuracy hypothesis with the warmup target fixed to the reference peak rate and the total update count held at 38. Run reference SGD and warmup SGD on the same paired train seeds and explore set, with the step rounding written in the config. Compare paired mean accuracy against the 1.0 pp threshold, and check that the update count and per-step learning-rate sum match between arms. A gap under 1 pp, or a gap explained by a learning-rate difference, counts against the idea.
missing_evidence: Source of code/toytrain/methods.py and code/configs/ (the brief's ../code/ path does not resolve in the reviewable tree)
Frozen reference SGD config (learning rate, schedule, seeds) and runner manifest
Exact warmup definition: target learning rate, rounding of the 10% window, post-warmup schedule
A stability measure (loss or update variance) if the 'steadier' claim is kept; none is declared in protocol.v1.json or metric-spec.v1.json
Power estimate showing that 3 paired seeds can detect a 1 pp accuracy difference on this synthetic task

document.title: critical_review CAND-0003
document.summary: claude_code anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5: proceed

named_risks: Peak-LR confound: the candidate does not fix the peak learning rate relative to the frozen reference LR, so a gain may reflect a larger LR rather than warmup (goal requires LR differences be excluded).
No warmup-free control at the same peak LR; warmup effect cannot be separated from peak LR without a constant-LR-at-peak arm.
Warmup step rounding is unspecified: 10% of 38 steps is 3.8, so warmup length may be 3 or 4 steps depending on implementation.
Protection metrics required by the goal's success condition are not defined in metric-spec.v1.json, which lists accuracy only; the success test cannot be applied as written.
Accuracy-only evaluation with n_eval=400 has 0.25 pp granularity; the 1.0 pp threshold equals four examples and accuracy may tie, while the goal asks for loss to be recorded as well.
Three search pairs with no seed-variance estimate may leave a 1 pp paired mean within noise.
Scope mismatch: the goal studies heavy-ball momentum, while CAND-0003 tests an LR schedule; a pass would not answer the goal's question and could use a limited confirmation slot (max 2 candidates).

Weak prior: LIT-0005 frames warmup benefit as dependent on sharpness and parametrization; logistic regression is convex, and the verified source does not support a fixed first-10% schedule or a single-task accuracy gain. A null result is the likely outcome.
Novelty and critical-review records referenced in the discovery file are not yet present, so the candidate has only one verified related paper (LIT-0005).
review_payload.cheapest_discriminating_experiment: On the frozen explore material and the three already-paired search seeds, run identical-data, 38-step arms: (A) reference SGD; (B) linear warmup over ceil(0.1*38) steps to a peak fixed in advance; (C) constant LR at the same peak with no warmup. Record paired accuracy and loss per seed. Proceed only if B-A >= 1.0 pp and B-C is not distinguishable from zero across seeds; if B-A is large but B-C is near zero, the gain is the peak LR, not warmup, and CAND-0003 should be abandoned.
missing_evidence: code/configs/reference.json (reference LR, batch size, optimizer settings) was not readable under the file-tool restriction and was not inferred.
code/toytrain/methods.py implementation of the schedule and step counting was not readable.
Definition of the protection metrics referenced by the goal's success condition, or confirmation that none apply.
The intended peak LR and post-warmup schedule for CAND-0003.
Rounding rule for warmup steps (3.8 steps for 38 total).
Seed-to-seed accuracy variance for this synthetic task, to judge whether a 1 pp paired mean over 3 pairs is meaningful.
A constant-LR-at-peak control arm, not mentioned in the candidate.
Novelty and critical-review records that the discovery file says remain required.

document.title: critical_review CAND-0003
document.summary: claude_code anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5: proceed

named_risks: Candidate wording is inconsistent: candidates.json line 6 and user-hypotheses.json line 8 describe cosine decay, while the title and refined-hypotheses.v2.md line 4 describe linear warmup over the first 10%. Revision 2 was created about 4 minutes after revision 1, so the spec may have shifted after the first review.

The peak learning rate is undeclared. If it differs from the reference learning rate (0.005 in the Zebra design), any accuracy gain is confounded with learning rate, which the constant-LR-at-peak control is meant to rule out.
Warmup over 10% of 38 updates is 3.8 steps. Without a fixed rounding rule (floor, ceil, or round) the schedule is not reproducible and the warmup length is ambiguous.
The post-warmup schedule is undeclared. A switch from warmup to cosine decay versus constant learning rate changes the comparison.

The 1.0 pp practical-gain threshold on a 400-example eval set (0.25 pp per example), averaged over only 3 paired seeds, is probably within seed-to-seed noise. A positive result may be a false positive, and a null result may be underpowered.
Retesting on the same explore split and seeds used for search risks selection bias. The protocol's confirmation on seeds 1042-1044 with independent c1 material is required before any GO claim.
The literature (LIT-0005) does not test this schedule or this task, so the novelty claim is only the narrow protocol test. Any wording that generalizes beyond the synthetic task would overclaim.
The reference configuration (code/configs/reference.json) could not be read, so the reference learning rate, step count, and schedule have not been checked against the Alpha design.
review_payload.cheapest_discriminating_experiment: Before any search run, write and freeze a spec that resolves the cosine/linear conflict and fixes the peak learning rate (equal to the reference rate), the rounding rule for 3.8 warmup steps, and the post-warmup schedule. Then run one small CPU sweep on the explore split over seeds 42-44 with three arms: reference SGD, warmup-then-constant at peak, and warmup-then-reference schedule. The warmup-specific claim survives only if warmup beats the constant-peak arm by more than 1.0 pp on paired accuracy. If the gain disappears against the constant-peak arm, the effect is peak learning rate, not warmup, and the hypothesis fails.
missing_evidence: Resolved candidate wording: a single statement of linear vs. cosine, and whether revision 2 supersedes revision 1 in user-hypotheses.json.
The frozen Alpha spec: peak learning rate, warmup-step rounding rule, post-warmup schedule, and the constant-LR-at-peak control arm.
Contents of code/configs/reference.json, to confirm the reference learning rate, step count, and schedule.
Whether code/toytrain/methods.py contains an Alpha implementation, and whether it matches the frozen spec.
The critical and novelty review files for CAND-0003 (cited only by name in the brief directory), to confirm they do not contradict this review.
Seed-level variance of explore accuracy under the reference configuration, to estimate whether a 1.0 pp paired gain on 3 seeds is distinguishable from noise.
Confirmation material c1 and its independence from the explore split, as required by protocol.v1.json.
